core.verdict: PASS. Core is genuinely robust: fault isolation, prototype-safe loading, the fixed-step accumulator, cost/refund math and number formatting all held up under a purpose-built scratchpad harness with zero errors attributable to the module and ~75k ticks/s. What keeps it below 9 is a handful of small correctness/polish edges — maxAffordable returns n-1 on exact-boundary money, fmt floors below 1000 but rounds above it, derived goes stale across loadState, sanitize wipes NaN money silently, and unlock side effects live inside read getters — each a few-line fix.
issues: [low] src/core/api.js:27-31 maxAffordable() is off by one when money exactly equals the n-purchase total: the closed-form floor(log(...)/log(g)) lands at n-1 through float error and the walk-back loop only ever decrements. Reproduced on 62 of 320 probes (e.g. house count=3 money=buildingCost(house,3,7) -> returns 6; apartment count=0 n=33 -> 32). In play this only bites when money is exactly on the boundary (sell refunds, round starting money), so the practical impact is a 'Max' button buying one fewer than affordable in rare cases. → After the walk-back add an upward walk: `while (n < 10000 && buildingCost(def, count, n + 1) <= money) n++;` (cap kept so g==1.0000001 cannot spin), or compute n via the closed form then adjust in both directions.

[low] src/core/format.js:30 floors values in [10,1000) but rounds above 1000, so fmt(999.99)='999' while fmt(999999)='1.00M' and fmt(999.5+0.5)='1.00K'. A player holding $999,999 sees '$1.00M' next to a $1.00M upgrade that reads 'not affordable'; and rates like +12.7/s display as '+12/s' (two significant figures) while 1.23K shows three. Inconsistent with Cookie Clicker/AD which round uniformly. → Either round everywhere (use roundFixed(n,0) for n>=10 and let tierFixed carry) or floor everywhere (in tierFixed, use Math.floor(v*p)/p) — pick one and apply it on both sides of 1000; consider fmt(n,1) for 10<=n<100 so rates keep three significant figures.

[low] src/core/state.js:79-86 loadState() replaces state but leaves `derived` (income, housing, powerRatio, mods) holding the previous run's values until the next tick; any UI read on the 'load' event before the next frame shows stale numbers, and derived.mods from the old run can leak into api.buildingCost via derived.costMult for one frame. → In loadState()/resetState(), reset derived to its defaults (or export a resetDerived() that zeros housing/jobs/power fields, sets costMult=1, mods=null) and have save/index.js call game.step(0) or a fold before emitting 'load'.

[low] src/core/state.js:115-118 sanitize() silently zeroes state.res.money/pop when they become NaN or Infinity (verified: money=-5 -> 0; 1e400 -> 0). A corrupted or overflowed value wipes the player's bank with no error entry, so the verify gate cannot see it happen. → Call reportError('sanitize', new Error(`res.${k} was ${v}`)) before the clamp so the anomaly lands in errors[] and console, and clamp Infinity to Number.MAX_VALUE rather than 0 for positive overflow.

[low] src/core/api.js:35-63 isBuildingUnlocked/isUpgradeUnlocked are called from the read-only listings buildings()/upgrades() but mutate state.unlocks and emit('unlock') as a side effect, so unlock toasts/logs fire from whichever caller (bot, UI render, tools) happens to list first, and a guard-disabled unlock (returns undefined) leaves the item locked for the rest of the session with no player-visible notice. → Move unlock evaluation into a tick handler (registerTickHandler('unlocks', ...)) that walks registry defs once per tick and emits there; make the api getters pure reads of state.unlocks. Surface guard.isDisabled() in the listing (e.g. `broken: true`) so the UI can grey the card.

[nit] src/core/state.js:63-76 mergeInto keeps unknown top-level keys (loadState({foo:{bar:1}}) -> state.foo persists and will be re-saved forever), and src/core/loop.js:110 stop() is never called anywhere in src/ (dead export) while loop.speed is a writable public field with no clamp. → Whitelist merge targets to Object.keys(createInitialState()) in loadState (the save module's scrub covers the browser path but core should be safe alone); either use stop() from hard-reset or drop it; clamp loop.speed to [0, 10] in frame().

balance.verdict: Measured from logs/sim-gauntlet.json, logs/gauntlet.json and two 3-h/12-h re-runs of tools/economy-sim.mjs: first building 0 s; first upgrade 4 s (Welcome Sign) / 48 s (Zoning Reform); first shop 86 s; first brownout 140 s; 1k pop 12-13 min; 10k pop 28 min; prestige panel 13.9 min, Found button arms 23.3 min, bot founds 39.9 min (5 legacy). Income $1.39/s @1 min, $13/s @3, $441/s @10, $51k/s @30, ~$1.2M/s peak at 40 min, $1.6e11/s @180 min, $2e19/s @12 h; growth before first prestige is x317 over minutes 1-10, x12.5 (10-20), x9.3 (20-30), x22.6 (30-39) — far above the DESIGN '10x/hour' sketch but bounded to <= x3 per minute after minute 3. Brownouts: 26% of verify samples under full power, 4% under 0.9, floor 0.89; 2.2% of the 12-h session. 68 foundings; cycles 39.9, 16.2, 15.8, 5.9, 5.3, 5.1, 4.4, 4.9, 4.3, 4.5, then lengthening 4.9 -> 11.1 over cities 11-24 and exactly 11.3 min for cities 25-68. All 20 buildings and all 82 upgrades are bought (civic-bonds-30 'never purchased' is a final-snapshot artifact). The first city is genuinely premium-quality pacing — no gap over 44 s in three hours, smooth income, well-spaced tier-4 decisions — but the 12-hour arc has a real gameplay flaw: from city 10 the prestige cadence decelerates and then locks to a timer-driven 11.3-min treadmill with zero new content and zero purchase tension (every item affordable within 2 s, cash = 2 s of income) for 9.5 of 12 hours, and power/happiness cease to matter after city 1. Plus one attributable error: the config revision broke two simulation tests by not updating the DEFAULTS mirror the config itself says to keep in step. Score 7.5 — solid, first-hour excellent, but a clear late-game pacing flaw and a shipped test break keep it below the 8.5 bar. FAIL.
issues: [high] Prestige cadence stops accelerating after city 10 and then locks: cycles lengthen 4.3 -> 4.9 -> 5.3 -> ... -> 11.1 min over cities 11-24, then run at exactly 11.3 min for 44 consecutive cities (hours 4-12). The length is pinned by a wall-clock timer, not the economy: Civic Bonds II-XXX open on a fixed issue schedule (src/upgrades/data.js BOND_OPEN_2=45 s, BOND_GAP=10 s + 0.8 s/rung, rung XXX at 10.5 min) and the city ripens ~50 s after the ladder ends (config.prestige.compoundPerMinute 0.1). config.js lines 28-33 and 209-221 admit this is 'the one pacing flaw left' and that no knob in config.js can fix it. Against the rubric (cadence accelerating, Antimatter Dimensions style), 9.5 of 12 hours are a countdown. → Move the bond schedule into config.js so balance owns it: `upgrades.horizon = { open2: 45, gap: 10, gapPerRung: 0.8, gapMin: 3 }` read by data.js bondOpensAt(), and scale gap by bank size, e.g. gap = max(gapMin, 10 - 2*log10(max(1, legacy/100))) so a 1e4-legacy city issues rungs every 6 s and a 1e6 city every 3 s, giving 11.3 -> ~7 -> ~5 min cycles instead of a flat 11.3. Re-measure with `node tools/economy-sim.mjs --ticks 432000` and require durations[24..68] to be monotonically non-increasing.

[high] No purchase tension after city 5: from city 6 onward the bot's max gap between purchases is 2 s in every city (my re-run, 12 h) and cash on hand is ~2 s of income (e.g. $4.1e19 money vs $2.0e19/s income at 12 h; $3.1e11 vs $1.6e11/s at 3 h). The last dollar-priced upgrade is planetary-charter at $3e12 (config.js line 398, bought by city ~20) while income reaches 1e19/s — seven orders of magnitude of price space with nothing to save for. Building growth 1.12-1.18 per unit vs x1.26 income per 11-min city means every building is spam-affordable. Cookie Clicker/AD keep a 'next big thing' at 5-30x current cash at all times; here it is 0 from hour 4 on. newFixed upgrades per city hits 0 at city 25 and stays 0 for 44 cities. → Add 6-8 more fixed rungs in config.upgrades spaced x30-x100 from $1e14 to $1e20 (e.g. 'dyson-swarm' 1e14, 'quantum-exchange' 3e15, 'mass-driver-port' 1e17, 'ringworld-district' 3e18, 'stellar-engine' 1e20) paired with new effects in the upgrades module, and/or raise cost.tierGrowth[4] 1.12 -> 1.15 and [3] 1.14 -> 1.16 so the frontier climbs faster than x1.26 per city. Target: in the 12-h sim every city after the 10th should show at least one purchase gap >= 30 s and one new fixed rung.

[medium] Power and happiness stop being mechanics after the first city. powerRatio is 1.000 in 97.8% of 60-s samples across the 12-h session and never dips under 0.9 after minute 5 of city 1 (session minima 0.738 at city-1 min 3, 0.847 at min 5); happiness sits at 2.3-2.8 (cap 3) from city 12 on. DESIGN.md lists power (loop step 3) and civic (step 4) as core pillars, but with nuclear 12k MW at $400k and fusion 60k MW at $4M (config.js lines 279-280, 326, 342) the grid is solved the moment each city hits 8k pop. → Make late demand outpace supply: raise config.buildings.financial powerUse 800 -> 2000 and arcology powerUse 500 -> 1200, and trim fusion powerGen 2e6 -> 3e5 (config.buildings.fusion), so a city 2+ that ignores power browns out at 20-30k pop. Target: session share of samples under ratio 1 rises from 2.2% to 8-12% with the floor never under 0.7.

[medium] Cities 2 and 3 are the same length (16.2 and 15.8 min) but city 3 is weaker than city 2 (peak income $2.1e7/s vs $6.1e7/s) — a fresh 10-legacy player experiences a second replay that is no faster and earns less than the first replay, before the sprint kicks in at city 4 (5.9 min). The shape 40 -> 16 -> 16 -> 6 is bumpy; a smooth 40 -> 20 -> 12 -> 7 would read as 'each city faster'. → Raise config.prestige.firstBonus 0.3 -> 0.4 only for the second city or, better, let Civic Bonds I open on $3e8 earned in-run instead of $1e9 (config-driven `upgrades.horizon.bondOneEarned`) so city 3 gets the bond sprint that city 4 currently gets. Target durations for cities 2-4: <= 14, <= 10, <= 7 min with peak income strictly increasing city over city.

[medium] Contract drift caused test failures: the balance revision changed startMoney 280->300, prestige.firstBonus 0.5->0.3, compoundPerMinute 0.08->0.1, compoundCap 1->1000, startMoneyPerLegacy 0.1->0.05 without updating the DEFAULTS mirror in src/simulation/tuning.js, breaking 2 of 31 simulation tests ('DEFAULTS mirror the shipped balance config' and the fallback/clamp test). config.js line 165-166 itself says 'keep its DEFAULTS in step with this block'. The integrator fixed it, but the error is attributable to this module's commit. → Stop hand-mirroring: have src/simulation/tuning.js import the shipped values (`import { config as shipped } from '../balance/config.js'`) and freeze `DEFAULTS = structuredClone(shipped.prestige)` at module load, keeping only the clamp ranges hand-written; or add `npm test` to the balance module's pre-commit checklist so a mirror mismatch cannot ship.

[low] First-minute feel: after the $300 opening spree the player sits with pop 16, jobs 0, happiness 0.70 (unemployment penalty), income $1.11/s flat from 20 s to 48 s waiting on the $50 Zoning Reform, then another 38 s for the $50 corner shop at 86 s. The shop unlocks at pop >= 4 (~10 s) but cannot be afforded for 75 s; the first thing the UI shows a new player is an 'unemployed/unhappy' city and a purchase they cannot make. → Bring the first paycheck under a minute: config.buildings.shop baseCost 50 -> 35 (keeps income 0.8) or economy.startMoney 300 -> 335 so the shop lands ~55-60 s and Zoning Reform ~70 s. Target: first shop < 60 s, longest no-purchase gap in minute 1 <= 30 s, happiness back above 0.85 by 90 s.

[low] 1k population arrives at 12.1-13 min against DESIGN.md's 'about 8 min' target; DESIGN.md's pacing paragraph is flagged stale but was never rewritten, so the two documents disagree on 1k pop (8 vs 13 min), $1M-earned (35-50 vs 18 min) and threshold ($1e6 vs $3e6). → Either pull towers forward (config.buildings.tower baseCost 3000 -> 2400, apartment 300 -> 260) to land 1k pop at ~10 min, or replace the DESIGN.md 'Pacing target' paragraph with the measured numbers from the config.js header (1k pop 13 min, $1M 18 min, Found arms 23 min, first founding ~40 min) so there is one contract.

resources.verdict: PASS. The resources module is correct, well-defended and fast: every formula was re-derived by hand from the real config and matched to the last digit, edge cases from pop 0 to 1e308 counts stay finite, the hot path allocates nothing, and derived.extra gives the UI a complete happiness/income breakdown. Remaining findings are documentation drift, a stale derived.mods reference on the null-mods path, an Infinity-pop inconsistency, and the duplicated DEFAULTS table - none affect gameplay or produced errors in verify/sim.
issues: [low] src/resources/index.js:305 `derived.mods = m === NEUTRAL_MODS ? derived.mods : m` leaves a stale mods bag on derived when a caller passes null mods: verified in scratchpad - after computeDerived(state, d, {income:5}) then computeDerived(state, d, null), d.mods still points at the income-5 bag while d.extra.incomeBreakdown.multiplier reflects neutral (0.826). Any consumer reading derived.mods (e.g. cost previews) sees numbers inconsistent with derived.income. → Set `derived.mods = m` unconditionally (NEUTRAL_MODS is frozen, so exposing it is safe), or document on computeDerived that derived.mods is only maintained when mods is supplied.

[low] src/resources/index.js:152 `nonNeg(state.res.pop)` maps pop = +Infinity to 0 (num() treats non-finite as missing) while every other overflow path clamps to FINITE_MAX via finite(). Verified: {pop: Infinity, house:1} yields income 0, growth +0.6 as if the city were empty - an inconsistent policy versus the 1e308 handling two lines later. → Read pop as `finite(nonNeg(...))`-style: `const p = state?.res?.pop; const pop = p === Infinity ? FINITE_MAX : nonNeg(p);` so a saturated pop behaves like the 1e300 case rather than vanishing.

[low] docs/DESIGN.md 'Resources' math section is stale relative to the shipped module: it does not mention pollutionCap/pollutionCurve saturation, mods.inflow, byBuilding.happiness, or the extra fields pollutionRaw/vacancy/openJobs/powerSurplus/happinessMult/incomeBreakdown.multiplier, and it still shows the linear pollution form. The building table also lists shop income 0.3 while config gives 0.8. → Update the DESIGN.md Resources math block to the saturating pollution formula and list the full derived.extra shape as computeDerived writes it (index.js:308-327); add a one-line pointer that config.js overrides the per-building numbers in the table.

[low] src/resources/index.js:93-108 DEFAULTS duplicates src/balance/config.js numbers (taxPerPop, wage, growthRate, civicCap ... 16 values). The drift test mitigates it, but it is still a second copy of tuning truth that a balance pass has to remember to touch, contradicting config.js's 'single source of tuning truth' header. → Keep only the two saturation keys (pollutionCap/pollutionCurve) in DEFAULTS as true fallbacks and derive the rest by importing config statically (the module already awaits '../balance/config.js' in init; a static import is DOM-free and removes the lazy-load race where computeDerived called before init() silently uses DEFAULTS).

[nit] src/resources/resources.test.mjs:289 `assert.equal(formatResource('pct', 1), '1')` tests an unknown resource id ('pct' is a format, not an id) and pins the fallback path by accident; it reads as a typo for formatResource('happiness', ...). → Replace with an explicit unknown-id assertion (`formatResource('nope', 1) === '1'`) plus the intended `formatResource('pop', 1234) === '1,234'`-style check.

[nit] computeDerived is documented as 'Pure' (index.js:2, 141) but reads the module-level `registry` singleton and the module-level `balanceConfig`, so it is not injectable for tests without registering synthetic buildings globally (which resources.test.mjs has to do, leaking 't-*' ids into the shared registry). → Accept an optional `buildings` map/order in the config or a 5th parameter defaulting to registry, and reword the header to 'Pure apart from reading registry and writing derived'.

buildings.verdict: The buildings catalogue is release-grade: 20 distinct roles across 5 categories and 4 tiers, all of them purchased in a 12h sim with zero errors, a new card every 2-4 minutes for the first 34 minutes, strong one-line flavor, and a defensive, well-tested registration layer with data-driven synergies. The one real gap is that those synergies' explanatory text never reaches the build card, so the module's most interesting design decision plays as unexplained number drift; fix that one UI line and tidy the stale comments and this is a 9.
issues: [medium] The signature mechanic is invisible to the player. data.js attaches `synergy.text` ('Income +20% per 1,000 citizens (up to x3)' etc.) to mall/refinery/techpark/financial and index.js publishes them via game.buildings.synergies, but `grep synergy src/ui/` returns nothing: src/ui/build.js renders only the housing/jobs/income/draw/joy stat rows (lines 108-113), so a mall's income number silently drifts from $40 to $120/s and the player is never told why or what to build to raise it. → In src/ui/build.js card builder, after the stat rows, render `def.synergy?.text` as a small italic hint line (e.g. h('div.card-synergy', { text: def.synergy.text })) and, for the 'building:<id>' sources, show the current factor ('x1.4') using synergyFactor from src/buildings/index.js so the bonus reads as live.

[low] Longest dead stretch in the first-city unlock cadence is 22m (hospital) -> 28m (techpark): six minutes with no new building card while income sits at $8k-19k/s. Every other gap is <= 4 min. → In src/balance/config.js lower the techpark popUnlock from 8,000 to ~6,000 (the bot has 6,000 citizens at 26 min) or add an intermediate tier-3 civic/commercial building; keep the $300k base cost so it stays affordable at unlock.

[low] Stale documentation inside the module: the data.js header (lines 38-41) says the financial district sits at '15-20 per $k' with income 2000, but config.js now owns financial at baseCost $2M / income 9000, and the arcology comment describes 2,500 housing while config trims it to 1,000. The DESIGN.md table is also stale (acknowledged there with a warning banner). → Rewrite the data.js 'Signature mechanics' paragraph to point at config.buildings for the tier-4 numbers, or move the financial income (9000) and arcology housing (1000) into data.js so the catalogue is the readable source and config only holds deltas.

[low] Windmill is a near-dead card after the first five purchases (costGrowth 2 -> 5th costs $640, 10th $20k) yet stays in the Power tab for the whole game with a live buy button; the sim still bought 53 of them at absurd prices in the late game because the bot scores any affordable item. → Either cap windmills (add an optional `max` field in data.js and have index.js/core refuse purchases past it, with the card showing 'Hilltops full 5/5') or soften costGrowth to ~1.5 in config.buildings.windmill so it remains a real early-game filler instead of a trap.

[low] Unlock hints for pop-gated tier-1/2 buildings do not use locale formatting consistently: 'Reach 250 citizens', 'Reach 500 citizens' pass, but the test only asserts the number is quoted for pop >= 1000, so a future override (e.g. popUnlock(4000,'4000')) would silently desync hint and mirror. → Derive the hint from the mirror in resolveBuilding (`Reach ${at.pop.toLocaleString('en-US')} citizens`) when unlockAt.pop is set and no explicit hint override is supplied, and drop the label parameter from config.js popUnlock.

upgrades.verdict: PASS at 8.5. The upgrades module is release-quality: 82 legible, individually meaningful rungs, unlock gates that verifiably fire (first city buys 30 upgrades by minute 37; every late city funds all 82 inside its 11-minute cycle), effects strictly confined to the mods bag under a deep-frozen-state test, zero errors, 13/13 tests. The income-priced, schedule-issued horizon ladder plus founding memory solve the two classic prestige-loop failures (nothing to buy late, click-spam after reset). The evidence's 'civic-bonds-30 never purchased' is not a defect - it is the final city being cut off at 9 min before rung XXX opens at 10.45 min; samples show 82/82 owned in earlier late cities. What keeps it below 9: thirty identical '+25% income' bond cards make the late cycle a treadmill, data.js cost literals and section headers have drifted from the shipped config ladder, Community Events is a weak standalone rung, and the bond desc leaks '2 s of income' jargon. All are cheap, targeted fixes.
issues: [medium] Late-cycle variety: Civic Bonds I-XXX are 30 identical '+25% income' cards (src/upgrades/data.js civicBond, lines 292-312). A late city's 11-minute cycle is ~44 decisions of which 30 are the same card, only broken by 5 Skyline Expansions. Benchmarks (Antimatter Dimensions, Kittens) vary repeatable ladders by effect. → Rotate the effect per rung within each 5-rung block (e.g. n%5: 1 income +25%, 2 growth +50%, 3 jobs +30%, 4 power x1.5, 5 income +25%) with matching descs/icons, keeping the same 2 s price and schedule so pacing pins in upgrades.test.mjs still hold.

[low] Doc drift: data.js header (line 22-24) says 'the defaults here match the tuned ladder in src/balance/config.js' and the late-game section is labelled '$120k - $5e8', but config.js lines 385-398 override 14 late rungs to a different ladder (skyway-frames 190000 vs 400000, digital-city-hall 3e5 vs 1.3e6, preventive-care 4.8e5 vs 4e6, robotic-assembly 7.7e5 vs 1.3e7, ..., planetary-charter 5e8 vs 3e12). Runtime is correct because config wins, but anyone reading data.js alone gets a ladder ~4-6000x too cheap. → Sync the data.js cost literals for those 14 ids to the config values (or delete the config overrides and keep one source), and change the section header to '$120k - $3e12'.

[low] Community Events (data.js line 447-457, $500) is the weakest rung: a lone +0.1 happiness, which at the h~0.85 it unlocks at is ~+6% income and ~+12% growth - under the module's own >=25% bar, only passing via the +0.1 happiness escape clause. → Pair it like Green Belts/Modern Curriculum do: compose(happier(0.1), global('growth', 1.25)) and desc 'Happiness +10% and population grows +25% faster'.

[low] Bond/Skyline desc text 'costs 2 s of income' / '2 s of income · opens 3 min after founding' (data.js lines 298-301, 320) is designer jargon in a player-facing 70-char line; the live dollar price is already on the Buy button (src/ui/upgrades.js line 110) and the schedule is already the unlockHint. → Shorten to 'All income +25% · price follows your income' (and for Skyline 'All housing and jobs +50%'), leaving the timing to unlockHint/unlockAt so the desc reads as an effect, not a spec.

[low] First-city cadence has three 3-minute stretches with no new upgrade (minutes 9-12, 16-19, 20-23 in logs/sim-gauntlet.json samples) while buildings keep landing every 6-16 s; the mid ladder $6k-$150k has 12 rungs spread over 25 minutes but the $20k-$50k band (night-shift, bulk-permits, container-port, tourism-board) clusters and then nothing until high-density/express-transit pop gates release. → Add one cheap ($2-4k) tier-2 residential/power rung gated on tower count or 20 MW demand around minute 9, and re-space night-shift/container-port to 15k/45k so a rung opens roughly every 90 s from minute 8 to 25.

simulation.verdict: The simulation module is technically excellent: correct fixed-dt integration with airtight clamps and NaN guards, an allocation-free tick that runs at 0.017 ms average (p99 0.10 ms), a complete event surface, a milestone system with careful replay semantics, and a prestige loop whose exploits (idle maturity, tap ripening, bonus-buys-bonus) are closed and covered by 31 passing tests; 0 errors are attributable to it. It narrowly misses the 8.5 bar on design polish rather than code: after hour four the loop settles into 43 identical 11.3-minute cycles with nothing new per founding, the legacy tier ladder runs out three hours before a session ends, and the in-file design docs quote figures (85k legacy, 1e15 money, 44-minute first founding) that are hundreds of times off the measured run. Fix the tier ladder and the stale headers and add one source of late-cycle variety and this is a 9.
issues: [medium] Late-game prestige loop becomes a metronome: from founding ~25 (hour ~4) every cycle in logs/sim-gauntlet.json is exactly 6760 ticks (11.3 min) for the remaining 8 hours, with the bank growing x1.25 per founding (7.4k -> 37.5M) and income rising a near-constant ~x1.12 each time. Nothing new is introduced per cycle, so the last two-thirds of a 12 h session is 43 identical resets. → Give late cycles variety from within this module: e.g. make compoundPerMinute or minGainShare step with legacy tiers (prestige.js requiredGain/compoundGainFor), or add a per-founding 'charter' choice (one of three temporary run mods) emitted with the 'prestige' event so replays differ. At minimum stretch the cycle over time (ripenSeconds > 0 scaled by legacy) so the loop slows as the bank saturates rather than repeating at a fixed period.

[medium] Legacy tier ladder in milestones.js ends at legacy-1m (1e6) but the 12 h sim banks 37.5M legacy; the last tier is reached around founding 52 (hour ~9), so the final ~16 foundings (3 hours) have no nextTierName/nextTierAt target on the dashboard, and foundingLine falls back to 'the income bonus holds at +X%' with no 'Next tier' clause. → Extend LEGACY_MILESTONES in src/simulation/milestones.js with legacy-10m (1e7) and legacy-100m (1e8) entries (or slow bank growth so 1e6 lands at hour 11+), keeping the ~x2.5-x10 spacing so a tier arrives every 4-10 foundings.

[medium] Design documentation in the module is stale by orders of magnitude: src/simulation/tuning.js header says 'first founding lands at ~44 min', 'Twelve hours end near 85k legacy (was 19M)'; src/simulation/prestige.js header says the soft cap 'keeps twelve-hour money in the 1e15 range'. Measured: first founding 39.9 min, 12 h legacy 37.5M, money 4.1e19-6.5e19. A balance owner tuning from these comments would be misled. → Re-measure with `node tools/economy-sim.mjs --ticks 432000` and rewrite the two header paragraphs (tuning.js lines 64-71, prestige.js lines 34-45) with the current figures, or replace the hard numbers with a pointer to logs/sim-gauntlet.json so the docs cannot drift.

[low] tuning.js documents legacyCapTail and legacyCapTailPower as 'config.prestige knobs read here', but src/balance/config.js prestige section does not define them (harmless today because legacyCap is 0, but the DEFAULTS-mirror contract is incomplete and the balance owner cannot see the knobs). → Add `legacyCapTail: 0.05, legacyCapTailPower: 0.3` to config.prestige in src/balance/config.js (with a one-line comment that they only bite when legacyCap > 0), or drop them from the documented list.

[low] GATES 'panel:prestige' in src/simulation/index.js line 113 hard-codes `prestigeTuning(config).threshold / 10` ($300k); the divisor is not a tuning knob and is invisible to the balance module, unlike every other pacing number the simulation reads. → Add `prestigePanelShare` (0.1) to config.prestige and DEFAULTS in tuning.js and read it in the gate.

[low] prestigeStatus is computed every tick for the dashboard even though nothing in it changes when totalEarned has not moved (e.g. a city with zero income); prestigeGain -> rawGainAt calls prestigeTuning ~6 times per evaluation, each doing a 16-key Object.is scan. Not a measurable cost today (avg 0.017 ms) but it is the only non-trivial per-tick work with no early-out. → In simulate(), skip prestigeStatus when state.stats.totalEarned and legacy are unchanged since the last call (two cached numbers), and let prestigeTuning cache by `config.prestige` identity first, falling back to the key scan only when the section object is the same but a knob may have changed.

ui.verdict: PASS at 8.5. The dashboard is premium-indie quality on every axis I could verify: coherent glass design system with category accents, tabular mono numerals, a skyline that genuinely grows and lives (day/night, windmills, smoke, window lights), diffed DOM writes with 0.45 ms average render cost at 60 fps, real buttons with visible focus, inline confirms instead of window.confirm, reduced-motion honored, and zero errors in the gauntlet or in my own 1440x900 and 1100x800 runs. Both widths lay out cleanly with no overflow or clipped text. It falls short of 9 on two concrete, reproducible flaws: unlock toasts re-announce (with nonsense counts) on every prestige run, and the three-high toast stack overlays Buy buttons in the build column at 1100x800, plus a cluster of small polish nits (icon-only tabs at 1440, clamped upgrade text without tooltip, power-chip rounding, hint flash on load).
issues: [medium] Unlock toasts re-fire on every prestige run and the batch count is not deduplicated. src/core/api.js isBuildingUnlocked/isUpgradeUnlocked emit 'unlock' whenever state.unlocks is re-latched, and src/ui/index.js pendingUnlocks is a plain array with suppression only on 'load'. Live run after 6 bot prestiges showed a toast reading '116 new buildings unlocked - Residential Tower, School and 114 more' and '347 new upgrades available' (game has 20 buildings / 80 upgrades). In real-time play every run re-announces 'New building: Apartment Block' etc. (38 runs in the 12h sim). → In src/ui/index.js: (1) make pendingUnlocks.buildings/upgrades Maps keyed by id so a burst never counts an id twice; (2) on the 'prestige' event set suppressUnlockToasts=true for ~1500 ms exactly as 'load' does, and additionally keep a Set of ids already announced this session (persist in state.settings or ui) so re-latches on later runs get the card glow but no toast.

[medium] Toast stack blocks build-card Buy buttons. styles.css .toasts is fixed at bottom:18px, left:53%, width 380px, MAX_VISIBLE=3 in src/ui/toast.js, so three toasts occupy y=679-882 at 1440x900 and y=579-782 at 1100x800 with pointer-events:auto. At 1100x800 with Cottage/Apartment/Tower unlocked (as in the gauntlet end state) the third card's Buy button (~y 610-660) sits under the first toast; a click dismisses the toast instead of buying. Bursts of three are common (milestone + buildings + upgrades land together). → Set MAX_VISIBLE to 2 and shrink toast padding to 9px 12px (saves ~70 px), or move the host to top-right of the build column (below the tab bar) where it only covers the onboarding note, or add padding-bottom to .col-build equal to the toast host height while toasts are present (toggle a class on .shell from show()/dismiss()).

[low] At the most common desktop width (1440) the build column measures 580 px, under the 600 px container query in styles.css (@container build (max-width: 600px)), so four of five category tabs collapse to icon+count and the names Commercial/Industrial/Power/Civic are never shown without hover (see logs/screenshot-gauntlet-mid.png and -end.png). The 32fr/42fr/26fr grid in .layout is what produces 580 px. → Change .layout grid-template-columns to minmax(320px, 30fr) minmax(380px, 44fr) minmax(300px, 26fr) (build column becomes ~607 px at 1440), or tighten .tab padding to 5px 7px and gap to 2px so five labelled tabs fit in ~565 px and lower the container threshold to 570px.

[low] Upgrade descriptions are clamped to 2 lines (.ucard-desc -webkit-line-clamp: 2) with no tooltip, so long legacy upgrade text is unreadable: live 1100 capture shows 'All income +50% × √legacy (+112% a...' for Dynasty Ledger and the 1440 capture shows the same truncation. → In src/ui/upgrades.js card(): set title: def.desc on the .ucard element (owned chips already do this), and raise the clamp to 3 lines for .ucard.cat-prestige, or shorten those descriptions in src/upgrades/data.js to fit two lines at 86px-button width.

[low] Power chip rounding is visibly inconsistent: logs/screenshot-gauntlet-mid.png shows '84 / 80 MW' with '3.25 MW spare' (84-80=4). src/ui/topbar.js formats cap and demand with short() (integer at that magnitude) but computes spare from the unrounded difference. The 'capacity / demand' order is also the reverse of the usual 'used / total' convention, and at <=1180px the sub-line is hidden so '72 / 53 MW' alone is ambiguous. → Format all three with the same precision (short(cap,1), short(dem,1)) or compute spare as short(Math.round(cap)-Math.round(dem)); consider '53 / 72 MW' (demand / capacity) with the fill bar meaning the same thing, and keep a compact sub like '+18' visible at narrow widths instead of hiding .chip-sub entirely.

[low] On page load with a saved city the 'tap the city to collect' pill flashes then fades: src/ui/hero.js applies .is-done only in update(), and styles.css transitions .city-hint opacity over 600 ms, so the pill is visible for the first frames of every session (faintly captured mid-fade at the bottom of the skyline in logs/screenshot-gauntlet-mid.png despite 53 taps). → Set the is-done class synchronously in createHero() from game.state.stats.clicks before the element is attached, or add `.city-hint.is-done { visibility: hidden; transition: opacity 600ms, visibility 0s 600ms }` and skip the transition on the first render (e.g. a .no-anim class removed after the first frame).

[low] City Log is the last panel in the scrolling side column; once Upgrades and Milestones populate it sits ~500 px below the fold (side column scrollHeight 1358-1627 vs 704-804 client) so the narrative log is effectively never seen after the first minute. → Cap .panel-milestones to RECENT=2 reached + UPCOMING=2, or move the log into the hero column beneath City Stats, or make .panel-log a collapsible details with a 'new entries' badge in the head.

[low] Tablist has ARIA roles but no arrow-key navigation (src/ui/build.js tabs are role=tab inside role=tablist but only click switches); there is no h1 on the page (brand-name is a span, panels are h2); the per-frame api.buildings()/api.upgrades() calls in src/ui/index.js render() spread ...def into ~100 fresh objects every frame (measured cheap at 0.45 ms avg, but it is avoidable GC churn). → Add a keydown handler on tabBar for ArrowLeft/ArrowRight/Home/End that calls setActive and focuses the tab; make .brand-name an h1 styled identically; have api.buildings()/upgrades() reuse a cached row object per id and only refresh count/cost/affordable/unlocked fields.

[low] City Stats grid (repeat(auto-fit, minmax(128px,1fr))) leaves a lone 'Taps' tile in a fourth row at 1440 (logs/screenshot-gauntlet-mid.png), and stat tiles carry no state colour, so 'Unemployment 82.8%' and 'Unemployment 54.8%' read as neutral data next to a 'Euphoric 188%' happiness chip. → Drop 'Taps' into the Settings > This city list (or merge into 'Total earned' sub-text) so the grid is 3x3, and add is-warn/is-bad classes on the unemployment tile (>25% warn, >50% bad) reusing the chip colour tokens.

save.verdict: PASS. The save module is production-grade: every requested scenario (play/save/reload restore, six garbage payloads plus a prototype-pollution attempt, 2 h offline catch-up with toast and 0.5x credit, export/import round trip, hardReset, throwing localStorage and quota errors, 30 s autosave plus 1.5 s debounced and unload saves) passed in a real Chrome session with zero console errors, and the code is defensive throughout (probeStorage try/catch, scrub + coerceShape + core sanitize double layer, corrupt-save parking, savedAt clamped to now, version stamping that never lies). Held back from 9.5 only by the small gaps above: debounced saves dropped during sub-30 s catch-ups, building purchases not on the debounced list, no unit tests for the pure parse/codec/migration functions, and the autosave toggle silently disabling unload saves.
issues: [low] src/save/index.js:544 — while catchUp.running, 'upgrade'/'milestone' events skip the debounced save on the assumption that catch-up ends with its own save, but finishCatchUp (line 300) only saves when seconds >= offlineMinSec (30). A short background-tab catch-up (e.g. 20 s throttling) that pops a milestone/upgrade therefore leaves the change unsaved until the next 30 s autosave. → In finishCatchUp, save when either seconds >= cfg.offlineMinSec OR a debounced event was suppressed during the run (track a `dirty` flag set in the DEBOUNCED_SAVE_EVENTS handler), or simply drop the `catchUp.running` guard so the 1.5 s debounce still fires.

[low] src/save/index.js:24 — DEBOUNCED_SAVE_EVENTS is ['upgrade','milestone'] only; 'buy'/'sell'/'prestige'-adjacent building purchases rely on the 30 s interval plus unload handlers. A tab/process crash (not a close) inside that window can replay up to 30 s of construction. Unload handlers were verified to work, so exposure is small. → Add 'buy' and 'sell' to DEBOUNCED_SAVE_EVENTS (the 1.5 s debounce already collapses a shopping spree into one 1.8 KB write).

[low] No unit tests for src/save/ although resources/ and simulation/ ship *.test.mjs. parseSave, encodePayload/decodePayload, runMigrations and coerceShape are pure exports and the empty MIGRATIONS table has no regression guard for the day STATE_VERSION bumps. → Add src/save/save.test.mjs (node:test) covering: garbage/hostile JSON -> {ok:false} reasons, __proto__ scrubbing, base64 round trip incl. urlsafe + whitespace, and a MIGRATIONS[1] stub asserting version stamps stop at the last runnable step.

[low] src/save/index.js:553-562 + src/ui/modal.js:175 — turning off 'Autosave every 30 s' also silently disables the visibilitychange/pagehide/beforeunload saves, so a player who unticks it and closes the tab loses the whole session unless they pressed 'Save now'. The setting label does not say this. → Either keep the unload saves independent of the autosave toggle (only the interval/debounce should honour it), or change the modal label/help text to 'Autosave (every 30 s and when you leave)'.

[high] Prestige cadence stops accelerating after city 10 and then locks: cycles lengthen 4.3 -> 4.9 -> 5.3 -> ... -> 11.1 min over cities 11-24, then run at exactly 11.3 min for 44 consecutive cities (hours 4-12). The length is pinned by a wall-clock timer, not the economy: Civic Bonds II-XXX open on a fixed issue schedule (src/upgrades/data.js BOND_OPEN_2=45 s, BOND_GAP=10 s + 0.8 s/rung, rung XXX at 10.5 min) and the city ripens ~50 s after the ladder ends (config.prestige.compoundPerMinute 0.1). config.js lines 28-33 and 209-221 admit this is 'the one pacing flaw left' and that no knob in config.js can fix it. Against the rubric (cadence accelerating, Antimatter Dimensions style), 9.5 of 12 hours are a countdown. → Move the bond schedule into config.js so balance owns it: `upgrades.horizon = { open2: 45, gap: 10, gapPerRung: 0.8, gapMin: 3 }` read by data.js bondOpensAt(), and scale gap by bank size, e.g. gap = max(gapMin, 10 - 2*log10(max(1, legacy/100))) so a 1e4-legacy city issues rungs every 6 s and a 1e6 city every 3 s, giving 11.3 -> ~7 -> ~5 min cycles instead of a flat 11.3. Re-measure with `node tools/economy-sim.mjs --ticks 432000` and require durations[24..68] to be monotonically non-increasing.

[high] No purchase tension after city 5: from city 6 onward the bot's max gap between purchases is 2 s in every city (my re-run, 12 h) and cash on hand is ~2 s of income (e.g. $4.1e19 money vs $2.0e19/s income at 12 h; $3.1e11 vs $1.6e11/s at 3 h). The last dollar-priced upgrade is planetary-charter at $3e12 (config.js line 398, bought by city ~20) while income reaches 1e19/s — seven orders of magnitude of price space with nothing to save for. Building growth 1.12-1.18 per unit vs x1.26 income per 11-min city means every building is spam-affordable. Cookie Clicker/AD keep a 'next big thing' at 5-30x current cash at all times; here it is 0 from hour 4 on. newFixed upgrades per city hits 0 at city 25 and stays 0 for 44 cities. → Add 6-8 more fixed rungs in config.upgrades spaced x30-x100 from $1e14 to $1e20 (e.g. 'dyson-swarm' 1e14, 'quantum-exchange' 3e15, 'mass-driver-port' 1e17, 'ringworld-district' 3e18, 'stellar-engine' 1e20) paired with new effects in the upgrades module, and/or raise cost.tierGrowth[4] 1.12 -> 1.15 and [3] 1.14 -> 1.16 so the frontier climbs faster than x1.26 per city. Target: in the 12-h sim every city after the 10th should show at least one purchase gap >= 30 s and one new fixed rung.

[medium] Power and happiness stop being mechanics after the first city. powerRatio is 1.000 in 97.8% of 60-s samples across the 12-h session and never dips under 0.9 after minute 5 of city 1 (session minima 0.738 at city-1 min 3, 0.847 at min 5); happiness sits at 2.3-2.8 (cap 3) from city 12 on. DESIGN.md lists power (loop step 3) and civic (step 4) as core pillars, but with nuclear 12k MW at $400k and fusion 60k MW at $4M (config.js lines 279-280, 326, 342) the grid is solved the moment each city hits 8k pop. → Make late demand outpace supply: raise config.buildings.financial powerUse 800 -> 2000 and arcology powerUse 500 -> 1200, and trim fusion powerGen 2e6 -> 3e5 (config.buildings.fusion), so a city 2+ that ignores power browns out at 20-30k pop. Target: session share of samples under ratio 1 rises from 2.2% to 8-12% with the floor never under 0.7.

[medium] Cities 2 and 3 are the same length (16.2 and 15.8 min) but city 3 is weaker than city 2 (peak income $2.1e7/s vs $6.1e7/s) — a fresh 10-legacy player experiences a second replay that is no faster and earns less than the first replay, before the sprint kicks in at city 4 (5.9 min). The shape 40 -> 16 -> 16 -> 6 is bumpy; a smooth 40 -> 20 -> 12 -> 7 would read as 'each city faster'. → Raise config.prestige.firstBonus 0.3 -> 0.4 only for the second city or, better, let Civic Bonds I open on $3e8 earned in-run instead of $1e9 (config-driven `upgrades.horizon.bondOneEarned`) so city 3 gets the bond sprint that city 4 currently gets. Target durations for cities 2-4: <= 14, <= 10, <= 7 min with peak income strictly increasing city over city.

[medium] Contract drift caused test failures: the balance revision changed startMoney 280->300, prestige.firstBonus 0.5->0.3, compoundPerMinute 0.08->0.1, compoundCap 1->1000, startMoneyPerLegacy 0.1->0.05 without updating the DEFAULTS mirror in src/simulation/tuning.js, breaking 2 of 31 simulation tests ('DEFAULTS mirror the shipped balance config' and the fallback/clamp test). config.js line 165-166 itself says 'keep its DEFAULTS in step with this block'. The integrator fixed it, but the error is attributable to this module's commit. → Stop hand-mirroring: have src/simulation/tuning.js import the shipped values (`import { config as shipped } from '../balance/config.js'`) and freeze `DEFAULTS = structuredClone(shipped.prestige)` at module load, keeping only the clamp ranges hand-written; or add `npm test` to the balance module's pre-commit checklist so a mirror mismatch cannot ship.

[low] First-minute feel: after the $300 opening spree the player sits with pop 16, jobs 0, happiness 0.70 (unemployment penalty), income $1.11/s flat from 20 s to 48 s waiting on the $50 Zoning Reform, then another 38 s for the $50 corner shop at 86 s. The shop unlocks at pop >= 4 (~10 s) but cannot be afforded for 75 s; the first thing the UI shows a new player is an 'unemployed/unhappy' city and a purchase they cannot make. → Bring the first paycheck under a minute: config.buildings.shop baseCost 50 -> 35 (keeps income 0.8) or economy.startMoney 300 -> 335 so the shop lands ~55-60 s and Zoning Reform ~70 s. Target: first shop < 60 s, longest no-purchase gap in minute 1 <= 30 s, happiness back above 0.85 by 90 s.

[low] 1k population arrives at 12.1-13 min against DESIGN.md's 'about 8 min' target; DESIGN.md's pacing paragraph is flagged stale but was never rewritten, so the two documents disagree on 1k pop (8 vs 13 min), $1M-earned (35-50 vs 18 min) and threshold ($1e6 vs $3e6). → Either pull towers forward (config.buildings.tower baseCost 3000 -> 2400, apartment 300 -> 260) to land 1k pop at ~10 min, or replace the DESIGN.md 'Pacing target' paragraph with the measured numbers from the config.js header (1k pop 13 min, $1M 18 min, Found arms 23 min, first founding ~40 min) so there is one contract.
